_comment: Model selection policy — WHICH model and WHICH effort for each kind of work, plus the catalog facts that make the choice checkable. router/policy.json owns ROUTING (task -> tier); this file owns the JUSTIFICATION and the dated facts behind it (price, context, retirement). scripts/model_policy_check.py enforces that the two agree and that nothing here has gone stale. Edit this file, not prose in a doc — a model choice buried in Markdown cannot be validated.
_review_note: Model capability moves faster than most standards. A dated review is the only thing that stops a tier map from silently describing last year's models. scripts/model_policy_check.py fails once reviewBy passes.

catalog._comment: Facts, not opinions. status: active | deprecated | retired. retiresOn is the published retirement date where one exists. Prices are USD per 1M tokens.

claude-fable-5.note: Most capable widely released. Thinking always on — omit the thinking param; an explicit disabled returns 400. No assistant prefill. Requires 30-day data retention (unavailable under ZDR). Safety classifiers can return stop_reason=refusal.

claude-opus-4-8.note: Default Opus tier. Strongest long-horizon autonomous execution. Adaptive thinking only.

claude-sonnet-5.note: Near-Opus quality on coding/agentic at Sonnet cost. Adaptive thinking on by default. ~30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 (new tokenizer) — re-baseline budgets, don't reuse old counts.

claude-haiku-4-5.note: Cheapest Claude. 200K context — the only current model under 1M. Simple, speed-critical work only.

claude-opus-4-1.note: Do not adopt. Migrate to claude-opus-4-8.

gemini-2.5-flash-lite.note: Free-tier lane for bulk deterministic-adjacent work. Cross-vendor: blocked for confidential scopes by policy.json risk.blockCrossVendor.

effort._comment: output_config.effort is a real cost/quality lever and is UNDER-USED — it moves spend more than model choice does on many tasks. Levels: low | medium | high | xhigh | max. Default when unset is high.

guidance.low: Short, scoped, latency-sensitive, not intelligence-sensitive. Also the right setting for narrow subagents.
guidance.medium: Cost-sensitive routine work where some capability tradeoff is acceptable.
guidance.xhigh: Best setting for most coding and agentic work on Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 5. Give max_tokens headroom (>=64000) — output truncates mid-thought otherwise.
guidance.max: Correctness matters more than cost. Diminishing returns and can overthink — test before committing.

workTypes._comment: Must stay in sync with router/policy.json taskTypes — model_policy_check.py enforces it. `why` is not decoration: an unjustified tier is how cost creeps.

classify.why: Fixed output space, no reasoning chain. A bigger model buys nothing measurable.

extract.why: Schema-bounded. Use strict tool use / structured outputs rather than a smarter model.

transform.why: Mechanical. Prefer t0 rules when the shape is stable.

route.why: A classification wearing a different hat.

summarize.why: Needs judgment about salience, but the output is checkable at a glance.

generate.why: Quality is user-visible; Sonnet 5 is near-Opus here at a third of the cost.

code-edit.why: Coding is the documented sweet spot for xhigh. Higher effort often REDUCES total cost by cutting turn count.

debug.why: Long tool-call chains; under-thinking here means more rounds, not cheaper rounds.

plan.why: Errors compound into everything downstream — the cheapest place to spend.

architect.why: Highest blast radius per token. Hardest to reverse once built on.

test-design.why: Tests are the verification substrate; a weak test suite hides failures everywhere else.

review.why: Adversarial reading is capability-sensitive. Cross-vendor verify is on for this type in policy.json.

selectionRules: Cheapest tier that clears the bar, not the best model available. The router picks the LOWEST tier a task needs.
Deterministic (t0) beats any model. If the shape is stable, write the rule — it is free, instant, and testable.
Raise EFFORT before raising TIER. Effort is a smaller, cheaper step and often the actual fix for shallow output.
Errors that compound justify a higher tier: planning, architecture, and review feed everything downstream.
Never route confidential-scope work cross-vendor. Enforced structurally by risk.blockCrossVendor, not by remembering.
Long-horizon agentic runs: give the FULL task spec in one well-specified first turn and run at high/xhigh. Ambiguous prompts revealed across turns cost more and perform worse.
Match max_tokens to effort. At xhigh/max set >=64000 or output truncates mid-thought.

reviewTriggers._comment: Events that force an OFF-CYCLE review, independent of reviewBy. The scheduled review catches drift; these catch shocks.
reviewTriggers.onNewModelRelease: Re-run the tier map: a new mid-tier often absorbs work from the tier above it.
reviewTriggers.onPriceChange: Intro pricing expiring is a price rise. See catalog introEndsOn.
reviewTriggers.onDeprecationNotice: Any catalog entry gaining a retiresOn date must be migrated before it lands.
reviewTriggers.onEvalRegression: A drop in eval/drift metrics (EVAL.md) may indicate a tier is now under-powered for its task type.
reviewTriggers.onPromptScaffoldingRot: Instructions written to work around an older model's limitation become pure overhead — and can REDUCE quality on newer models. Re-test scaffolding after a tier change.
